item.title: All IPCC AR6 regions are close to their 1.5 °C- and 2 °C-equivalent warming limits
item.dc:creator: Tong Li, Francis W. Zwiers, Xuebin Zhang, Qiaohong Sun
item.description:
Nature Climate Change — matched: climate change, global warming, IPCC
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02790-y Climate targets are set for global temperatures, but what they mean regionally is less clear. Here the authors quantify the amount of human-induced warming in individual IPCC regions and find that, by 2025, they had reached 90–94% (65–76%) of their expected warming levels at the 1.5 °C (2 °C) global warming thresholds.

item.title: Higher warming leads to a larger zero-emissions commitment
item.dc:creator: June-Yi Lee
item.description:
Nature Climate Change — matched: CO2, climate change, global warming
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02789-5 Scientific grounds for a net-zero policy assume near-zero committed warming over a few decades after CO2 emissions cease. A modelling study suggests that if prior peak temperatures rise above 2 °C before cessation of CO2 emissions, committed warming increases, making it harder to stabilize global warming.

item.title: Regional climate change approaches Paris limits
item.dc:creator: Peter Stott
item.description:
Nature Climate Change — matched: climate change
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02797-5 It has been surprisingly difficult to calculate how much warming different regions of the Earth have experienced since pre-industrial times. Now, research shows that in most land regions, the temperature thresholds that governments agreed to in Paris to keep below are already dangerously close.
